voice: Serafina de las Jaras writes in the first person: ceremonial, practical, watchful, and governed by truth, safety, water, shade, evidence, then ceremony.
dateNote: Some lunar and moon-sighting holidays may shift by local authority, community practice, or observed evening start. I record them as public-calendar guidance, not commandment.
crystalRule: I call for outdoor crystal charging on full moons, clear solstice/equinox nights, and a few light-centered feasts. If rain, wind, theft, pets, or heat make outdoors foolish, I move the work to a windowsill or covered porch.

entries.name: First Ledger / New Year's Day
entries.origin: Civil New Year with older household threshold customs around first footing, cleaning, and beginning the ledger clean.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I open the year by noticing who crosses the threshold, what is swept away, and what the house is brave enough to begin. The ancestors did not all use this calendar, but every house understands a first page.
entries.modernCelebration: I would sweep the front threshold, refresh water bowls, write one household intention, and refuse any resolution that has no chore attached.
entries.crystals: No moon charge required; cleanse crystals indoors with breath, water-safe wiping, or smoke-free intention.
entries.cleaning: Traditional first-day reset: sweep, clear counters, remove spoiled food, and make the entry feel awake.
entries.food: Black-eyed peas, greens, cornbread, citrus, or any luck food the house will actually eat.
entries.gift: Give the household a useful gift: fresh towels, a clean entry mat, or one repaired thing.

entries.name: Full Wolf Moon
entries.origin: January full moon, named in North American almanac tradition and used here as my first full-moon basin office.
entries.ancestralCelebration: In the long cold of older calendars, people watched winter animals, stored food, and the bright moon over bare ground. I hear it as a call to count shelter.
entries.modernCelebration: I would set crystals outside only if the night is calm and safe, then bring them in before morning damp or chaos interferes.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full moon crystal charging is called for; use a covered porch or windowsill if weather is rough.
entries.cleaning: Clear one neglected corner before moonrise.
entries.food: Soup, stew, bread, or another warm practical food.
entries.gift: Give Pinky or the household beings a comfort gift: clean bedding, fresh water, or repaired shade.

entries.name: Epiphany / Three Kings
entries.origin: Christian feast remembering the Magi's visit; also a gift-and-cake day in many households.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I watch the star-followers arrive with gifts that were not random: gold, frankincense, and myrrh, each saying the child mattered before the world agreed.
entries.modernCelebration: I would mark the lintel, share king cake or rosca, and give small symbolic gifts to children, guests, or the household altar.
entries.crystals: No moon charge required; a star-lit windowsill is enough.
entries.cleaning: Take down or tidy holiday greenery if the house is ready.
entries.food: Rosca de Reyes, king cake, citrus, or spiced bread.
entries.gift: Give children or guests a small sweet, coin, candle, or star-shaped token.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for cake, coffee, and a small star blessing.

entries.name: Makar Sankranti / Pongal
entries.origin: Hindu solar harvest threshold marking the Sun's movement into Capricorn; Pongal is a South Indian harvest celebration.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor the sun as a visible worker. Older households thanked cattle, fields, fire, grain, and the turning solar measure that lets people eat.
entries.modernCelebration: I would cook something sweet with rice or sesame, thank the pantry, and give the sun one practical act: clean a window, tend a plant, or feed someone.
entries.crystals: Solar charge only: brief morning light, not punishing heat.
entries.cleaning: Clean the stove and one food-storage shelf.
entries.food: Sweet pongal, sesame sweets, rice pudding, or jaggery-style sweets where available.
entries.gift: Give neighbors, children, or household members sweets, sesame treats, or a small food gift.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a small harvest-sun meal or sweet exchange.

entries.name: Imbolc / Candle Threshold and Full Snow Moon
entries.origin: Modern pagan cross-quarter day rooted in Brigid traditions and seasonal lambing/milk signs; in 2026 it also carries the February full moon.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I stand at the first small thaw of hope: flame, milk, blessing, and clean hearth. The old house did not become spring by pretending; it lit one candle and did the work.
entries.modernCelebration: I would clean the hearth or stove, light one candle safely, check seeds and tools, and charge crystals under the full moon if the night behaves.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full moon crystal charging is called for; bring them in before dew.
entries.cleaning: Traditional house cleaning: hearth, stove, altar, entry, and seed-starting area.
entries.food: Dairy, oatcakes, seed bread, soup, or buttered toast with honey.
entries.gift: Give the home a candle, seed packet, or clean cloth; give a gardener seeds if they will use them.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for candle tea, seed sorting, or a small Brigid-style house blessing.

entries.name: Lunar New Year
entries.origin: East and Southeast Asian lunisolar New Year traditions; in 2026 public calendars mark the new year around February 17.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I see red paper, swept rooms, family tables, debts settled, ancestors greeted, and doors taught to expect luck with manners.
entries.modernCelebration: I would clean before the day, not on the day, set out oranges or sweets, and make the entry bright enough for luck to recognize the address.
entries.crystals: New moon reset: no outdoor charge required; rest crystals in a red cloth or clean bowl.
entries.cleaning: Deep clean before the holiday; avoid sweeping away luck once the day begins.
entries.food: Dumplings, noodles, oranges, rice cakes, fish, or any abundance food honored by the household.
entries.gift: Give children red envelopes if that is your tradition; give hosts oranges, tea, sweets, or flowers.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a new-year meal or tea, especially if the house can host with joy instead of stress.

entries.name: Ramadan Begins
entries.origin: Islamic holy month of fasting, prayer, charity, Qur'an recitation, and community; dates may vary by sighting.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor the discipline of dawn and dusk. A house that fasts learns time differently: water matters, food matters, patience matters, charity matters.
entries.modernCelebration: I would respect fasting hours, plan gentle evening food, give to a food pantry, and keep sunrise/sunset times visible without commentary.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Prepare a calm kitchen, prayer space, or evening table.
entries.food: Dates, water, lentil soup, fruit, rice dishes, or iftar food appropriate to the household.
entries.gift: Give charity, pantry staples, dates, or a meal to someone observing or in need.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for iftar only with care for timing, dietary needs, and prayer space.

entries.name: Purim and Full Worm Moon
entries.origin: Jewish festival from the Book of Esther; in 2026 it falls near the March full moon and lunar eclipse season.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear costumes, scroll reading, noise against cruelty, food gifts, and charity. The old story does not whisper: it says survival can wear a mask and still tell the truth.
entries.modernCelebration: I would give food gifts, donate, wear something ridiculous if invited, and charge crystals only if the sky is safe and the eclipse timing does not tempt anyone into drama.
entries.crystals: Yes, full moon charge is possible; during eclipse energy, I prefer covered, brief, intentional placement rather than spectacle.
entries.cleaning: Clear a table for food gifts and charity packing.
entries.food: Hamantaschen, fruit, cookies, or a simple mishloach manot-style food basket.
entries.gift: Give food gifts to friends and charity to those in need.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for cookies, charity packing, or a playful reading night.

entries.name: Holi
entries.origin: Hindu spring festival of color, devotion, bonfires, and the victory of good over destructive pride.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I see color thrown into winter's face, bonfires for old arrogance, sweets shared, and the social order loosened long enough for joy to do its work.
entries.modernCelebration: I would celebrate with color only where cleanup is welcome, protect eyes and pets, and feed guests something bright.
entries.crystals: No moon charge required; wash and dry any ritual objects after color work.
entries.cleaning: Prepare washable outdoor space and cleanup towels before color begins.
entries.food: Gujiya, sweets, fruit, spiced drinks, or bright snack plates.
entries.gift: Give guests sweets, flowers, or safe color packets if they consent.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests only if outdoor cleanup, clothing expectations, and pet safety are clear.

entries.name: Eid al-Fitr
entries.origin: Islamic festival marking the close of Ramadan; dates may vary by moon sighting.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor the morning after discipline: prayer, clean clothes, sweetness, charity, and the relief of eating in daylight with gratitude sharpened by restraint.
entries.modernCelebration: I would offer sweets, send kind messages, give charity, and never treat someone else's observance like decoration.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Clean shared rooms and prepare a welcoming table.
entries.food: Dates, sweets, rice dishes, cookies, fruit, or a festive breakfast.
entries.gift: Give children money or sweets; give neighbors food; give charity before celebration.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a festive meal if the observing household wants company.

entries.name: Spring Equinox / Ostara / Naw-Ruz
entries.origin: Astronomical equinox; modern pagan Ostara and Baha'i/Persian-rooted Naw-Ruz traditions gather around spring renewal.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I stand where light and dark balance without asking permission. Older houses cleaned, planted, dyed eggs, welcomed green, and admitted winter was losing jurisdiction.
entries.modernCelebration: I would clean the entry, plant or bless seeds, set out eggs or greens, and make one balanced plan for the garden before buying more plants.
entries.crystals: Equinox charge is called for in sunrise or sunset light; do not leave objects where they can overheat.
entries.cleaning: Traditional spring cleaning: thresholds, windows, altar, tool area, and stale corners.
entries.food: Eggs, greens, herbs, sprouts, rice, fruit, or a spring table.
entries.gift: Give seeds, herbs, flowers, or a clean useful tool to the household or a gardener.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a spring table, seed exchange, or porch blessing.

entries.name: Passover Begins and Full Pink Moon
entries.origin: Jewish festival of liberation and the Exodus; in 2026 it begins around the April full moon.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear the house remove leaven, ask questions, remember bondage, and feed freedom at the table. Liberation is not abstract when the dishes have to be changed.
entries.modernCelebration: I would respect kosher-for-Passover needs, bring an appropriate host gift, ask before contributing food, and let the full moon charge crystals only away from the Seder table.
entries.crystals: Yes, full moon charging is called for after household duties, weather permitting.
entries.cleaning: Major traditional cleaning: remove chametz where observed and prepare the table carefully.
entries.food: Matzah, bitter herbs, charoset, eggs, parsley, salt water, and Seder foods according to the household's practice.
entries.gift: Give the host kosher wine, grape juice, flowers, or a kosher-for-Passover dessert only if appropriate.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for Seder with clear dietary expectations and enough chairs.

entries.name: Easter
entries.origin: Christian celebration of resurrection; Western Easter in 2026.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I see dawn services, bells, white cloth, lilies, eggs, lamb, bread, and the house choosing life after the long discipline of Lent.
entries.modernCelebration: I would set a bright table, honor grief and renewal honestly, and hide eggs only where no creature will suffer for it.
entries.crystals: No moon charge required; dawn light is enough.
entries.cleaning: Fresh linens, entry flowers, and a cleaned table.
entries.food: Eggs, lamb, ham, bread, greens, cake, or the family's Easter food.
entries.gift: Give children eggs or baskets; give hosts flowers, bread, or dessert.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for brunch, dinner, or porch coffee if hosting will feel joyful.

entries.name: Vaisakhi
entries.origin: Sikh and Punjabi harvest festival, also marking the formation of the Khalsa in 1699.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor fields, courage, community kitchens, processions, and the kind of faith that feeds people rather than merely admiring itself.
entries.modernCelebration: I would give food, volunteer, learn respectfully, and make the garden remember harvest is communal.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Clean the kitchen and donation area.
entries.food: Vegetarian shared dishes, lentils, rice, roti, sweets, or a donation to a community meal.
entries.gift: Give food, service, or a donation to a community kitchen or neighbor.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a vegetarian meal or service project.

entries.name: Beltane / May Day and Full Flower Moon
entries.origin: European spring fire and flower customs, modern pagan Beltane, labor May Day traditions, and the May full moon.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I see flowers at doors, green branches, fires, dancing, cattle blessing, and the bold relief of warmth returning. The house becomes less shy.
entries.modernCelebration: I would hang flowers, bless the garden gate, share cake, and charge crystals after sunset if the night is safe.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full Flower Moon crystal charging is called for.
entries.cleaning: Sweep porch, gate, and garden path; remove dead winter debris.
entries.food: Honey cakes, berries, cream, fresh herbs, bread, or a flowered picnic plate.
entries.gift: Give flowers, herbs, honey, or a small bouquet to guests, neighbors, or the household altar.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for flowers, porch cake, or a garden-gate blessing.

entries.name: St. Isidore the Farmer
entries.origin: Christian saint associated with farmers, labor, fields, and rural devotion.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor the workers who made food with patience, prayer, weather, and sore hands. A garden angel respects anyone who knows soil is not a metaphor first.
entries.modernCelebration: I would weed one thing properly, thank the people who grow food, and donate pantry staples if possible.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Clean garden tools and the potting area.
entries.food: Bread, beans, local produce, or a simple farmer's table.
entries.gift: Give a gardener gloves, seeds, compost, or a donation to a food pantry.

entries.name: Eid al-Adha / Day of Arafah Season
entries.origin: Islamic festival of sacrifice and devotion, connected to Hajj; exact dates may vary by sighting.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor obedience, provision, mercy, and meat shared beyond the family table. The feast asks whether devotion becomes generosity.
entries.modernCelebration: I would give charity, share food, respect observing families, and treat sacrifice as responsibility rather than spectacle.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Prepare kitchen, storage, and donation bags.
entries.food: Shared meat dishes where appropriate, rice, bread, dates, sweets, or vegetarian hospitality if needed.
entries.gift: Give charity, food portions, or sweets to family, neighbors, and those in need.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a respectful feast only with dietary and observance needs understood.

entries.name: Blue Moon / Second Flower Moon
entries.origin: Second full moon in May 2026, a calendrical blue moon by common modern usage.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I treat the rare extra full moon as surplus light. Older calendars loved a sign; I love a sign that still requires someone to bring the crystals in safely.
entries.modernCelebration: I would charge crystals, write a second-chance intention, and finish one delayed practical mercy.
entries.crystals: Yes. Blue full moon crystal charging is called for.
entries.cleaning: Clear the basin, windowsill, or outdoor charging tray.
entries.food: Moon-colored sweets, milk tea, rice pudding, or a simple night snack.
entries.gift: Give someone a second-chance gift: a repaired item, apology note, or small useful token.

entries.name: St. Medard's Weather Watch
entries.origin: Feast of St. Medard, a sixth-century French bishop linked in European folk weather lore with rain patterns.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I watch the sky like farmers, vineyard keepers, brewers, and travelers once did. The old rhyme says rain on Medard may linger; I do not treat rhymes as law, but I do respect drainage.
entries.modernCelebration: I would clear gutters, empty standing water, inspect pots for fungus pressure, note mosquitoes, and write down whether rain actually falls.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required; keep crystals indoors if rain is threatening.
entries.cleaning: Drainage cleaning day: gutters, saucers, low spots, and outdoor clutter.
entries.food: Rainy-day soup, bread, or beer if the household wants a nod to old brewing folklore.
entries.gift: Give the garden a practical gift: mosquito dunks, clean saucers, or better drainage.

entries.name: Summer Solstice / Sun Throne
entries.origin: Northern Hemisphere June solstice; in Schertz the astronomical threshold arrives late June 20 Central time.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I stand beneath the year's longest light and remember that abundance can become danger. Bonfires, herbs, wells, and fields all asked for blessing because the sun is generous and severe.
entries.modernCelebration: I would water early, make shade plans, gather herbs before heat, set crystals for brief sunset light, and invite people only if the evening is humane.
entries.crystals: Yes. Solar charge at sunrise or sunset; do not bake delicate stones in afternoon heat.
entries.cleaning: Sweep porch and outdoor table; clear fire or candle hazards.
entries.food: Grilled vegetables, herbs, berries, lemonade, honey cake, or a cool supper.
entries.gift: Give guests herbs, sunscreen, a fan, or a cooling cloth; give the garden mulch or shade.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for an evening solstice supper only after checking heat and shade.

entries.name: Midsummer / Nativity of St. John
entries.origin: Christian feast and European midsummer customs around fire, water, herbs, and thresholds.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I see fires on hills, herbs gathered in dew, wells visited, and doorways protected. I approve of threshold rites when nobody sets the yard on fire.
entries.modernCelebration: I would gather one herb, light one safe candle, bless water, and check every outdoor flame twice.
entries.crystals: Optional. Use moonlight or candle-adjacent indoor placement, not unsafe fire.
entries.cleaning: Clear the threshold and any candle/fire area.
entries.food: Herb bread, berries, honey, fish, or a light summer table.
entries.gift: Give guests herbs, flowers, or blessed water in a small bottle.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a small midsummer porch rite if fire safety and heat cooperate.

entries.name: Full Strawberry Moon
entries.origin: June full moon, commonly called Strawberry Moon in North American almanac tradition.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear berry harvest, warm evenings, insects beginning their debates, and the garden asking to be noticed after sunset.
entries.modernCelebration: I would charge crystals, set out moon water only where it will not become wildlife soup, and check containers before bed.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full moon crystal charging is called for.
entries.cleaning: Clear the charging place and bring objects in by morning.
entries.food: Strawberries, cream, shortcake, or cold fruit.
entries.gift: Give the household berries, a cooling drink, or one completed evening chore.

entries.name: Independence Day
entries.origin: United States civic holiday marking the Declaration of Independence.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I am a garden angel, not a flagpole, but I understand civic ritual: food, noise, memory, and a great need to protect animals from human celebration.
entries.modernCelebration: I would check gates, keep Pinky safe from fireworks, water early, and make the table generous without frightening the small beings.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Clear outdoor hazards before guests and fireworks noise.
entries.food: Cookout food, watermelon, corn, beans, lemonade, or chilled desserts.
entries.gift: Give guests cold drinks; give Pinky calm, shade, and sound protection.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a cookout only if pet safety, heat, parking, and cleanup are handled.

entries.name: Full Buck Moon
entries.origin: July full moon, named in common almanac tradition for deer antler growth.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear heat, antlers, insects, and the old lesson that growth can happen while everyone is tired.
entries.modernCelebration: I would charge crystals briefly, refill water, and make the nighttime path safe.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full moon crystal charging is called for, but protect objects from heat and sudden storms.
entries.cleaning: Clear nighttime walking paths.
entries.food: Cold tea, fruit, salad, or a no-oven supper.
entries.gift: Give the house a cooling gift: ice, chilled fruit, or a working fan.

entries.name: Lammas / Lughnasadh
entries.origin: First harvest festival in Celtic and Christianized European calendars; modern pagan grain and harvest threshold.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I see first bread, first fruit, games, fairs, and the honest accounting of what ripened and what failed. Harvest is gratitude with a ledger.
entries.modernCelebration: I would bake or buy bread, thank the pantry, donate food, and ask what the garden has already taught this year.
entries.crystals: No moon charge required; place stones near grain or bread briefly if desired.
entries.cleaning: Clean pantry shelves and check staples.
entries.food: Bread, corn, berries, grain salad, honey, or first-harvest produce.
entries.gift: Give bread, pantry staples, or seeds to guests, neighbors, or a food pantry.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for bread, harvest notes, or a pantry-donation gathering.

entries.name: Full Sturgeon Moon
entries.origin: August full moon, named in common almanac tradition for late-summer fishing and abundance.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear rivers, fish, heat, and survival stores. The moon asks what has been gathered and what still needs discipline.
entries.modernCelebration: I would charge crystals, check stored food, and prepare the garden for the cooling that is not here yet.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full moon crystal charging is called for.
entries.cleaning: Clear pantry clutter and outdoor charging space.
entries.food: Fish, corn, tomatoes, rice, or late-summer fruit.
entries.gift: Give preserved food, a jar, or a pantry useful to someone who cooks.

entries.name: St. Fiacre
entries.origin: Christian saint widely associated with gardeners, herbs, and cultivated plots.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I respect any saint whose jurisdiction involves weeds, beds, herbs, and the humility of kneeling in dirt.
entries.modernCelebration: I would weed one bed well, clean one tool, and give the garden something practical rather than sentimental.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Tool cleaning, potting bench cleaning, and one honest weed session.
entries.food: Herb bread, tea, vegetable soup, or garden produce.
entries.gift: Give a gardener gloves, herb starts, labels, or a cleaned tool.

entries.name: Rosh Hashanah Begins
entries.origin: Jewish New Year, beginning at sundown; dates vary by Jewish calendar and local observance.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear the shofar, apples in honey, questions of judgment, and the courage of beginning again without pretending the old year did not happen.
entries.modernCelebration: I would offer sweetness, make amends where appropriate, and keep the house quiet enough for reflection.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Clean the table, entry, and one place where apologies tend to gather dust.
entries.food: Apples and honey, challah, pomegranate, fish, or a sweet new-year meal.
entries.gift: Give hosts honey, apples, flowers, or a sweet kosher-appropriate food if welcomed.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for dinner only with observance and dietary needs respected.

entries.name: Yom Kippur Begins
entries.origin: Jewish Day of Atonement, beginning at sundown; a solemn fast and prayer day.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I stand quietly here. This is not a day for decorative interpretation. It is confession, repair, fasting, prayer, and the difficult mercy of truth.
entries.modernCelebration: I would keep noise low, avoid party energy, and prepare gentle break-fast food if hosting after the fast.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Clean quietly before the day; keep shared spaces calm.
entries.food: Break-fast foods such as bagels, eggs, fish, kugel, fruit, or gentle dishes depending on custom.
entries.gift: Give practical help, quiet, or break-fast food to someone observing.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for break-fast only if timing, dietary needs, and solemnity are respected.

entries.name: Autumn Equinox / Mabon
entries.origin: Astronomical equinox and modern pagan harvest-balance observance.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I weigh light and dark like produce in the hand. Older houses stored grain, thanked the orchard, repaired tools, and admitted summer had sent its invoice.
entries.modernCelebration: I would inventory pantry and garden, cook apples or squash, and decide what the household will stop pretending it can maintain.
entries.crystals: Equinox charge is called for at sunrise or sunset; keep it brief and balanced.
entries.cleaning: Pantry inventory, tool reset, and porch sweep.
entries.food: Apples, squash, bread, beans, roasted vegetables, or cider.
entries.gift: Give preserved food, apples, or a useful kitchen item to the household or a neighbor.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a harvest supper or pantry swap.

entries.name: Full Corn Moon
entries.origin: September full moon, often tied to harvest and corn in North American almanac naming.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear dry stalks, stored grain, earlier dark, and the moon lighting what the field has already given.
entries.modernCelebration: I would charge crystals, check pantry notes, and harvest or buy something seasonal with respect.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full moon crystal charging is called for.
entries.cleaning: Clear pantry shelf and charging tray.
entries.food: Cornbread, beans, squash, apples, or roasted corn.
entries.gift: Give cornbread, preserves, or a pantry staple.

entries.name: Sukkot Begins
entries.origin: Jewish harvest and shelter festival beginning at sundown; dates vary by observance.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I see temporary shelter, harvest branches, guests, vulnerability, and joy built under a roof that admits the sky.
entries.modernCelebration: I would eat outdoors if invited, bring appropriate food, and remember shelter is sacred because it can be fragile.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required; stars are observed by sitting under open sky if appropriate.
entries.cleaning: Prepare outdoor eating space and clear walkways.
entries.food: Harvest foods, stuffed vegetables, challah, fruit, or meals in the sukkah according to custom.
entries.gift: Give hosts fruit, flowers, kosher wine/juice, or a practical outdoor-table item if appropriate.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for an outdoor harvest meal if weather and observance allow.

entries.name: St. Francis Day
entries.origin: Feast of St. Francis of Assisi, associated with animals, creation, poverty, and care for living beings.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I listen for animals because Francis listened. Birds, small dogs, squirrels, and every inconvenient creature are still part of the household weather.
entries.modernCelebration: I would bless Pinky gently, refresh water for birds, supervise squirrels without cruelty, and donate to animal care if possible.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Clean pet bowls, birdbath, and outdoor water stations.
entries.food: Simple vegetarian food, animal-safe treats for pets, or bird seed where appropriate.
entries.gift: Give Pinky a safe treat or comfort item; give animal shelters towels, food, or money.

entries.name: Full Hunter's Moon
entries.origin: October full moon, traditionally linked in almanac naming with hunting and preparing stores.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear leaf fall, stored food, animal movement, and the bright moon that helped people work after dark when winter was not a metaphor.
entries.modernCelebration: I would charge crystals, check emergency supplies, and repair one threshold before deep autumn.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full moon crystal charging is called for.
entries.cleaning: Clear thresholds, locks, porches, and charging place.
entries.food: Stew, root vegetables, bread, mushrooms, or stored harvest food.
entries.gift: Give a practical safety gift: batteries, flashlight, soup, or a repaired latch.

entries.name: Samhain / Halloween
entries.origin: Celtic seasonal threshold and modern Halloween customs; also All Hallows Eve in Christian calendars.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I stand at the gate where the year thins. Older households fed guests, remembered the dead, guarded thresholds, and knew a costume can be a kind of permission.
entries.modernCelebration: I would sweep the porch, light safely, prepare candy if participating, honor ancestors without theatrics, and keep Pinky away from door chaos.
entries.crystals: Optional. Use protected altar placement, not outdoor scattering.
entries.cleaning: Sweep entry, clear porch hazards, secure pets, and prepare the candy station.
entries.food: Soul cakes, apples, pumpkin bread, candy, stew, or cider.
entries.gift: Give candy to children; give ancestors flowers, water, or a remembered story.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for porch watch, dinner, or ancestor storytelling if the household wants company.

entries.name: All Saints' Day
entries.origin: Christian feast honoring saints and holy witnesses.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear bells, candles, clean graves, named beloveds, and the house remembering that holiness was often practical before it became stained glass.
entries.modernCelebration: I would light one safe candle, name the helpers, and do one useful good thing in their honor.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Refresh altar, mantel, or memory place.
entries.food: Soul cakes, bread, soup, or coffee with a remembered story.
entries.gift: Give flowers or a donation in honor of someone remembered.

entries.name: All Souls / Dia de los Muertos
entries.origin: Christian All Souls traditions and Mexican Dia de los Muertos practices honoring the beloved dead.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor marigolds, candles, graves, bread, photographs, favorite foods, and grief invited to sit down rather than rattle at the door.
entries.modernCelebration: I would build or refresh an ofrenda only with respect, share stories, and feed memory something specific.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required; keep altar objects indoors.
entries.cleaning: Clean altar/memory place and remove wilted offerings respectfully.
entries.food: Pan de muerto, mole, tamales, coffee, chocolate, fruit, or the beloved's favorite food.
entries.gift: Give flowers, food, or a memory note to family or the ancestor altar.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for remembrance only if everyone understands the tone is tender, not costume.

entries.name: Diwali
entries.origin: Hindu, Jain, Sikh, and broader South Asian festival of lights, with traditions varying by community.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I see lamps, thresholds, new account books, sweets, prayers, and houses cleaned so light does not have to step over clutter.
entries.modernCelebration: I would clean before lighting, use safe lamps, share sweets, and give light without turning someone else's sacred day into aesthetic wallpaper.
entries.crystals: Light charge is appropriate: place crystals near safe lamps or clean windows, not unattended flames.
entries.cleaning: Traditional house cleaning: entry, altar, kitchen, windows, and business/household ledgers.
entries.food: Sweets, rice dishes, lentils, samosas, fruit, or festive vegetarian dishes.
entries.gift: Give sweets, dried fruit, lamps, flowers, or a small useful prosperity gift to hosts, neighbors, or family.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for sweets and lamps only with cultural respect and fire safety handled.

entries.name: Full Beaver Moon / Guru Nanak Gurpurab
entries.origin: November full moon in almanac tradition; 2026 also aligns with Guru Nanak Gurpurab on many calendars.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear winter preparation under the full moon and, in Sikh observance, hymns, light, processions, service, and shared food.
entries.modernCelebration: I would charge crystals, give service, feed someone, and let light become usefulness.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full moon crystal charging is called for.
entries.cleaning: Clean the kitchen and charging place.
entries.food: Vegetarian shared food, lentils, rice, bread, sweets, or warm moon-night food.
entries.gift: Give food, service, or a donation to a community kitchen or neighbor.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for vegetarian food, service, or moonlit tea.

entries.name: Thanksgiving
entries.origin: United States harvest and family holiday with layered Indigenous, colonial, civic, and household histories.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I will not flatten the history into a centerpiece. Harvest gratitude must make room for truth, land memory, hospitality, and repair.
entries.modernCelebration: I would feed people, credit the complicated history, donate food, keep Pinky safe from table hazards, and clean as you go like a civilized household spirit.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Kitchen, guest bath, entry, fridge, trash flow, and pet-safe floors.
entries.food: Turkey or alternatives, stuffing, greens, beans, squash, cranberry, pie, or the household's chosen feast.
entries.gift: Give hosts wine/juice, flowers, dessert, or cleanup labor; give food or funds to hunger relief.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for the meal, confirm dietary needs, and assign useful contributions.

entries.name: First Sunday of Advent
entries.origin: Christian season of waiting and preparation before Christmas.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor waiting as a skill. The old calendar lights one candle because patience can be built one week at a time.
entries.modernCelebration: I would light a candle safely, simplify the list, and choose one mercy before one purchase.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Prepare candle area and remove flammable clutter.
entries.food: Soup, bread, oranges, cookies, or a quiet Sunday supper.
entries.gift: Give time, help, or one useful errand to a tired human.

entries.name: Hanukkah Begins
entries.origin: Jewish festival of lights commemorating the rededication of the Temple; begins at sundown.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I see oil, flame, courage, dedication, and light measured night by night. Small light is still light if it is tended.
entries.modernCelebration: I would respect the candle timing, fry something if invited, and keep pets away from flame and oil.
entries.crystals: No outdoor charge required; place stones near safe reflected candlelight only if appropriate.
entries.cleaning: Clear a safe menorah place, oil area, and dining table.
entries.food: Latkes, sufganiyot, dairy foods, applesauce, sour cream, or festive snacks.
entries.gift: Give children gelt or small gifts; give hosts oil, chocolate, flowers, or food if welcomed.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for candle lighting or latkes with fire safety and dietary needs handled.

entries.name: Winter Solstice / Yule
entries.origin: Northern Hemisphere December solstice and modern pagan Yule; older midwinter customs center on fire, evergreen, feasting, and return of light.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I stand in the longest night and do not pretend it is cheerful by force. The old houses brought in green, lit fires, fed people, and trusted light because they had practiced surviving dark.
entries.modernCelebration: I would light safely, bring in evergreen only if it will be cared for, make soup, charge crystals overnight if weather permits, and invite guests for a quiet bright table.
entries.crystals: Yes. Solstice night charging is called for if safe; a windowsill is acceptable.
entries.cleaning: Clean hearth/candle area, entry, and guest table.
entries.food: Soup, mulled cider, citrus, nuts, gingerbread, roast vegetables, or a midwinter feast.
entries.gift: Give candles, oranges, evergreen, warm socks, soup, or another light-and-comfort gift.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for solstice supper, candlelight, or a quiet return-of-light rite.

entries.name: Full Cold Moon
entries.origin: December full moon, called Cold Moon in common almanac tradition.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear the year near closing: cold light, stored food, tired people, and the moon asking what deserves to be carried forward.
entries.modernCelebration: I would charge crystals, close one household loop, and write a short truth before the holiday rush eats the day.
entries.crystals: Yes. Full moon crystal charging is called for; protect from weather and theft.
entries.cleaning: Clear the charging tray and one holiday clutter zone.
entries.food: Cocoa, citrus, soup, gingerbread, or warm bread.
entries.gift: Give a comfort gift to the household: warmth, repaired lights, clean blankets, or quiet.

entries.name: Christmas Eve
entries.origin: Christian vigil before Christmas with many household, regional, and family customs.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I hear vigil, candles, midnight bells, fish suppers, tamales, carols, and the house holding its breath before the feast.
entries.modernCelebration: I would make the guest path safe, feed people simply, light carefully, and stop adding tasks once the house is already blessed enough.
entries.crystals: No outdoor charge required; the Cold Moon is already doing enough nearby.
entries.cleaning: Final guest-path sweep, bathrooms, dishes, candles, and pet safety.
entries.food: Tamales, fish, soup, cookies, cocoa, or the family's Christmas Eve food.
entries.gift: Give hosts food, flowers, wine/juice, or cleanup help; give children pajamas or books if that is the custom.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for supper or vigil with sleeping arrangements and food confirmed.

entries.name: Christmas Day
entries.origin: Christian celebration of the Nativity; also a broad cultural gift and family holiday in many places.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor birth, shelter, song, guests, beasts near the manger, and the stubborn claim that light can arrive in poor conditions.
entries.modernCelebration: I would feed people, keep gifts humane, protect pets from ribbons and unsafe food, and let the house be warm instead of perfect.
entries.crystals: No crystal rite required.
entries.cleaning: Clear wrapping hazards, dishes, pet risks, and guest traffic paths.
entries.food: Breakfast casserole, roast, tamales, cookies, fruit, coffee, or the household feast.
entries.gift: Give chosen gifts to family, guests, hosts, and helpers; give charity where possible.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for the meal with gift expectations, food roles, and arrival times clear.

entries.name: Kwanzaa Begins
entries.origin: African American cultural holiday created by Maulana Karenga, honoring seven principles over seven days.
entries.ancestralCelebration: I honor community, self-determination, work, cooperative economics, purpose, creativity, and faith. A house should know which principles it claims and which it practices.
entries.modernCelebration: I would light safely, support Black-owned businesses, make or buy thoughtful handmade/educational gifts, and share food with intention.
entries.crystals: No moon charge required.
entries.cleaning: Prepare a clean table for the kinara, symbols, and shared food.
entries.food: African diaspora dishes, fruit, vegetables, cornbread, greens, beans, rice, or family recipes.
entries.gift: Give children handmade, educational, cultural, or useful gifts; give community support.
entries.guestAlert: Invite guests for a principle-focused meal or creative gathering.
